PC: Immediately performs primary survey on arrival
Obtains full set of vital signs including rectal temperature
Performs a focused history and physical (focused neurological exam with Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS))
Provides initial AMS workup/intervention (Dextrose, O2, Naloxone, Thiamine)
Intubates patient with rapid sequence intubation (RSI) upon recognition of airway compromise
Appropriately addresses unstable vitals (warmed fluids for hypotension and hypothermia, may try atropine for bradycardia but should not attempt pacing due to hypothermia)

Obtains appropriate laboratory studies for patient with altered mental status and unstable vitals (Complete blood count (CBC), comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP), troponin, coagulation studies (PT/INR), lactate, type and screen, urinalysis (UA), thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH), urine drug screen (UDS), acetaminophen (APAP), Aspirin (ASA), ethanol (EtOH))
Obtains other studies as indicated (chest x-ray (CXR), computed tomography (CT) head, electrocardiogram (ECG))
Gathers essential and accurate informationfrom patient/EMS (history of illness,initial vitalsigns in the field, symptoms, severity,duration).
Sequences critical actions in patient care:vital signs,ABCs, primary survey, intubation,establishes IV/IO x2,AMPLE history, fluidresuscitation,orders and interprets radiographs.
Reevaluates patient after fluid bolus and re-warming and if vital signs start to deteriorate afterinitial stabilization.
MK: Describes an appropriate differential, plan, anddisposition.
SBP: Arrange for definitive care in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU)
Can handle distractions while maintainingpatient care priorities.
ICS: Instructs team to initiate key actions (Intravenous access (IV), Oxygen (O2), Monitor, etc)
Introduces self and efficiently establishesrespectful and effective communication withpatient/EMS.
Communicates clearly, concisely,andprofessionally with staff regarding interventions,radiology, lab orders,and consults.
